name: Business Consultant
seoTitle: Business Insurance Cost for Business Consultants
seoDescription: Business consultants pay about $265/yr for General Liability, $445 with E&O. See how bad-advice claims, scope disputes, and leaked client data drive cost.

industryContext.contextNote: Business consultants advise clients on strategy and operations without producing physical work product, so exposure centers on the advice itself rather than premises or equipment risk.

riskFactors.title: Advisory Negligence Claims
riskFactors.description: A client who acts on flawed strategic recommendations and suffers financial loss can pursue a professional negligence claim against the consultant.

riskFactors.title: Contract & Scope Disputes
riskFactors.description: Ambiguous statements of work or missed deliverables can trigger breach-of-contract claims requiring legal defense.

riskFactors.title: Confidential Data Exposure
riskFactors.description: Consultants routinely handle sensitive client financials and internal plans, creating liability if that data is leaked or breached.

faqs.question: Why do business consultants need Errors & Omissions insurance?
faqs.answer: E&O coverage protects consultants against claims that their advice or analysis was negligent, inaccurate, or failed to deliver the promised business outcome, even when the consultant acted in good faith.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a business consultant?
faqs.answer: A solo consultant in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $265 per year for baseline General Liability coverage; adding Errors & Omissions raises that total.

faqs.question: Does a business consultant need Cyber Liability coverage?
faqs.answer: Yes. Consultants who store client financial data, strategy documents, or access client systems remotely face data-breach exposure that General Liability does not cover.

faqs.question: Is General Liability enough for a business consultant?
faqs.answer: General Liability covers third-party bodily injury and property damage, but it excludes claims arising from professional advice. Most consultants pair it with Errors & Omissions for full protection.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Business consultants carry a 1.0 actuarial risk factor, reflecting minimal physical hazard offset by meaningful professional-advice liability exposure.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with annual revenue tier, team headcount, and whether Errors & Omissions or Cyber Liability endorsements are added to the base General Liability policy.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Business consulting premiums sit near the market midpoint — higher than low-touch creative freelancers, but well below hands-on trades like electricians or contractors.
